modules.name: sample_data
modules.doc:
Synthetic, realistic brand-lift survey data with confounded exposure.

Exposure (``group`` = "Exposed"/"Control", ~40% exposed) depends on age,
gender, region, income, media usage, prior brand usage, device and ad
blocking. The same factors drive the KPIs, so raw exposed-vs-control
differences overstate the true effect. True exposure effects (latent scale):

* aided_awareness   +0.45 log-odds
* unaided_awareness  0 (NO effect: any raw lift is pure confounding)
* favorability      +0.25 on the latent 1-5 scale
* consideration     +0.35 log-odds
* purchase_intent   +0.30 latent (ordered logit)
* ad_recall         +0.90 log-odds

modules.name: matching
modules.doc:
Greedy nearest-neighbour matching on logit(PS) with caliper, ratio,
replacement and exact-match strata.

Exact strata are handled by offsetting the matching distance of each stratum
by a large constant, so a single sorted search can be used for all strata
while never pairing units from different strata.

fields.name: treated
fields.description: index (into input arrays) of the focal unit

fields.name: weight
fields.description: 1 / (number of matches of the focal unit)

members.name: match_one_direction
members.signature: (score: ndarray, focal: ndarray, pool: ndarray, caliper: Optional[float], ratio: int = 1, replacement: bool = True, strata: Optional[ndarray] = None) -> propensity_lift.matching.MatchPairs
members.doc:
Match each focal unit (boolean mask ``focal``) to up to ``ratio`` units of
``pool`` (boolean mask) by nearest ``score`` within ``caliper`` (absolute,
same scale as score) and within identical ``strata``.

With replacement, pool units tied with the ``ratio``-th nearest distance are
all used and share the focal unit's weight (so a focal unit may get more than
``ratio`` matches, each weighted 1/n_matches).

fields.name: weights
fields.description: unnormalised: exposed 1 if matched; control sum of 1/k

fields.name: n_control_matched
fields.description: ATE: controls with an exposed counterpart

members.name: nn_match
members.signature: (logit_ps: ndarray, t: ndarray, caliper_abs: Optional[float], ratio: int = 1, replacement: bool = True, strata: Optional[ndarray] = None, estimand: str = 'ATT') -> propensity_lift.matching.MatchResult
members.doc:
Nearest-neighbour matching producing analysis weights.

ATT: exposed weight 1 (if matched), control weight = sum over the exposed it
serves of 1/k (k = matches of that exposed unit; = times used / ratio).
ATE: matched in both directions; each unit's weight = 1 (if it found a
counterpart) + its usage as a counterpart.

modules.name: doubly_robust
modules.doc:
Doubly robust (AIPW) estimation: an outcome regression plus an IPW correction of its residuals.

For each arm ``a`` an outcome model ``m_a(x) = E[Y | X = x, T = a]`` is fitted on that arm, then

    mu_a = mean over the target population of m_a(X)  +  IPW-weighted mean over arm ``a`` of (Y - m_a(X))

and lift = mu_1 - mu_0. The estimate is consistent when EITHER the propensity model or the outcome
model is correctly specified. The target population is everyone for the ATE and the exposed for the
ATT; with ATT weights (exposed = 1) the exposed-arm model cancels, so ``mu_1`` is the observed
exposed mean and only ``m_0`` has to be fitted.

Like lift.py, everything is computed for K outcomes and G row-groups at once.

fields.name: se
fields.description: G x K  influence-function SE of the lift (with_se=True)

members.name: fit_outcome_models
members.signature: (X: ndarray, Y: ndarray, M: ndarray, t: ndarray, binary: Sequence[bool], sample_weight: ndarray, arms: Sequence[int] = (0, 1)) -> Tuple[ndarray, ndarray]
members.doc:
Per-arm outcome regressions on ``X``: logistic for binary outcomes, linear otherwise.

Returns ``(m0, m1)``, both n x K: the predicted outcome of EVERY row under control / exposure.
``sample_weight`` (n,) selects and weights the rows used for fitting (0 = not used, bootstrap
multiplicities otherwise); rows with a missing outcome (``M == 0``) are never used. An arm that
is not in ``arms`` is returned as zeros.

members.name: aipw_estimate
members.signature: (w: ndarray, q: ndarray, t: ndarray, D: ndarray, Y: ndarray, M: ndarray, m0: ndarray, m1: ndarray, with_se: bool = False) -> propensity_lift.doubly_robust.AipwEstimate
members.doc:
Augmented IPW means for weights ``w`` (IPW weights, 0 for rows left out) and target weights ``q``.

``q`` (n,) defines the population the outcome-model predictions are averaged over: 1 for every
analysed row (ATE) or for the analysed exposed rows only (ATT), times any bootstrap multiplicity.
Weights are self-normalised (Hajek), so ``w`` and ``q`` need no particular scale.

schemas.doc:
Shared data contracts for propensity_lift.

This module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the shapes exchanged between
the analysis package, the FastAPI backend and the React frontend
(frontend/src/api/types.ts mirrors these models 1:1, snake_case preserved).

Terminology
-----------
* exposed / control  : the two respondent groups, read from ``treatment_column``.
* model_features     : covariates fed to the propensity-score model.
* matching_features  : columns the respondents were (or should be) matched on.
                       Used as EXACT-MATCH strata for nearest-neighbour matching,
                       and always reported in balance / overlap diagnostics.
                       Numeric matching features with > 10 unique values are
                       coarsened into quintiles before exact matching.
* outcome_columns    : brand-lift KPIs (awareness, favourability, consideration,
                       purchase intent ...). Binary outcomes are reported as
                       proportions; others as means.
* overlap / underlap : on the propensity-score scale (and per feature), the
                       region where BOTH groups have support is the overlap;
                       regions where only one group has support are underlap
                       ("exposed_only" = exposed respondents with no comparable
                       controls, "control_only" = controls unlike any exposed).

fields.name: control_values
fields.description: None => every other non-missing value is control

fields.name: outcome_positive_values
fields.description: Optional recode of outcomes to binary, e.g. top-2-box: {"purchase_intent": ["Very likely", "Somewhat likely"]} -> 1 if in list else 0

fields.name: caliper
fields.description: matching in SDs of logit(PS); None = no caliper

fields.name: weight_clip
fields.description: weighting opt-in cap on IPW / AIPW weights at this per-group quantile (0.99 = p99); None = no clipping (unbiased)

fields.name: missing_strategy
fields.description: for features; rows with missing outcome are dropped per-outcome

fields.name: n_dropped_treatment_missing
fields.description: treatment value missing / in neither group

fields.name: feature
fields.description: source column name (encoded dummies are aggregated back)

fields.name: importance
fields.description: abs standardized coef (logistic) or impurity importance, normalised to sum 1

models.name: OverlapSummary
models.doc: Propensity-score over/underlap (computed on the pre-trim sample).

fields.name: n_trimmed_exposed
fields.description: removed by the trim rule (0 if trim == "none")

fields.name: pct_exposed
fields.description: 0-100, share of the exposed group in this region

models.name: Histogram
models.doc: Shared bin edges; counts and densities per group (len(edges) == len(counts)+1).

models.name: FeatureOverlap
models.doc: Raw-data over/underlap for one model or matching feature.

fields.name: overlap_coefficient
fields.description: OVL of the two empirical distributions

fields.name: pct_exposed_unsupported
fields.description: % exposed whose value never occurs / is outside control range

fields.name: effective_n_control
fields.description: Kish ESS for weighted methods, matched n otherwise

fields.name: exposed_mean
fields.description: proportion (0-1) for binary; AIPW: model-based, may fall slightly outside

fields.name: caliper_abs
fields.description: caliper on logit scale actually used
